newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares surge to new peak, more records seen.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares surge to new peak, more records seen.

text.p: The top-20 KFX Danish share index blazed ahead to hit a new all-time closing high for the seventh consecutive trading day on Wednesday with dealers foreseeing more moderate advances on Thursday.
"Provided that the Dow holds up and the dollar stays strong, the general market optimism should persist with new if more modest gains tomorrow," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index finished 1.47 point higher at 180.48, the 41st record closing high of the year, while the KFX August future rose 2.70 point to 181.70 with 130 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Total bourse turnover was 1.3 billion crowns.

SAS and Copenhagen Airports rose on better than expected June passenger traffic figures and a Swedish newspaper report that SAS might switch domestic Swedish flights to and from Malmo, south Sweden, to nearby Copenhagen when a bridge and tunnel connecting the cities opens in the year 2000.
SAS later said that it had no such plans.
Its share closed 2.50 crowns higher at 85.50, while Copenhagen Airports put on a hefty 25 crowns to end the day at 750.00. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969650
